description: Printer auto-detection database with Klipper hardware fingerprints
_field_variant_of: Optional on a printer entry: the id of the entry for the same machine without this entry's firmware mod or add-on, which "variant_label" (required alongside it) names in a few words, e.g. "ForgeX" or "CFS". A saved-vs-detected type warning between an entry and its base, or two variants of one base, is worded as that difference rather than as two different printers. A base entry carries neither field.
_field_image_variants: Optional on a printer entry: an ordered list of alternate images chosen by hardware the app detects on the connected printer, each {"when": {<condition>: <value>, ...}, "image": "<file in assets/images/printers/>"}. The first variant whose every condition holds replaces the entry's image; none holding leaves the plain image, and a custom image the user picked always wins. Conditions: filament_system - a detected filament system of this kind that the app presents, as AmsSystemInfo::presents_filament_system() decides (tool_changer is not a filament system and never matches), spelled as ams_type_from_string() parses it (cfs, afc, happy_hare, ace, ad5x_ifs, snapmaker, qidi_box, openams). A condition key or value this build does not know makes its variant never match, and the [printer_database][schema] test fails on one, so a misspelling cannot ship silently. The image re-resolves when detection changes, so a filament system registering after connect switches it live.

heuristic_types.hostname_exclude: Exclude this printer if the hostname matches this pattern
heuristic_types.kinematics_match: Match against printer kinematics type (corexy, cartesian, delta, etc.)
heuristic_types.kinematics_exclude: Exclude this printer if kinematics matches (e.g. cartesian excludes corexy-only brands)
heuristic_types.object_exists: Check if a Klipper object exists in /printer/objects/list (substring; '^' pins the pattern to the start of a name and '$' to its end, so '^box$' is exactly the object 'box')
heuristic_types.stepper_count: Count of Z steppers (z_count_1, z_count_2, z_count_3, z_count_4)
heuristic_types.led_required: Exclude this printer if the LED list was reported and lacks the pattern. Absence as evidence, for a sibling that differs from this entry only by hardware it carries; a list that was not reported yet never excludes.
heuristic_types.sensor_required: As led_required, over temperature sensor names
heuristic_types.fan_required: As led_required, over fan object names
heuristic_types.object_required: As led_required, over the full Klipper object list
heuristic_types.led_exclude: Exclude this printer if an LED matching the pattern is present. The counterpart of led_required, for the sibling that lacks the hardware.
heuristic_types.sensor_exclude: As led_exclude, over temperature sensor names
heuristic_types.fan_exclude: As led_exclude, over fan object names
heuristic_types.object_exclude: As led_exclude, over the full Klipper object list
heuristic_types.mcu_match: Match against MCU chip type or serial pattern
heuristic_types.build_volume_range: Match against the X/Y stepper travel Klipper resolves from the configfile (position_max minus position_min per axis), not the bed mesh or the advertised print area. Travel is the print area plus whatever overtravel the config allows (the four entries authored from a real config show +10 to +58 mm), so a window drawn tightly around the marketing size misses the machine it describes; author min/max from a real configfile. A heuristic setting "measure": "declared_bed" matches the bed size the firmware config declares instead of travel
heuristic_types.macro_match: Match against G-code macro names (gcode_macro objects)
heuristic_types.macro_exclude: Exclude this printer if a G-code macro is present
heuristic_types.tool_count: Count of extruder tools (tool_count_1, tool_count_2, tool_count_4)
heuristic_types.cpu_arch_match: Match against host CPU architecture string
heuristic_types._modifier_corroborating: Set true on a heuristic whose evidence names a CLASS of printer rather than a model: a chamber thermistor (every enclosed machine has one) or an MCU claimed by more than one model. The flag is per-entry authoring - vendor hostnames stay identifying where an entry authors them as model signals and corroborate where it does not. It can never be the base score and adds nothing to the match bonus, so it cannot identify a printer or separate look-alikes on its own; it supports through match_count and the separator opt-in.
heuristic_types._modifier_identifying: Set true on a build_volume_range whose window is distinctive enough to lead. Volumes are corroborating by default because models overlap in the common bands; this opts an unusual size back in. It still needs the entry's kinematics to match, so a size alone never names a printer.
heuristic_types._modifier_measure: Set to "declared_bed" on a build_volume_range to match its window against the bed size the firmware's own config declares (Creality: gcode_macro product_param variable_bed_size_x and variable_bed_size_y) instead of stepper travel. Travel also covers overtravel to a purge or nozzle-clean position, so a declared bed suits a window that has to tell apart models whose travel overshoots their beds (K2 Plus against K2 Pro). A firmware that declares no bed size never matches such a window; nothing falls back to travel. Any other value matches nothing.
heuristic_types._modifier_separator: Set true on a corroborating heuristic whose evidence names the model within a family the entry's other heuristics identify: a bed size (K2 Plus against K2 Pro) or an MCU part number separating vendors whose class evidence ties. A match adds its weight to the uncapped score - the margin between look-alikes - once the entry's non-separator base clears the autosave bar; it never raises the published confidence and never becomes the base, so a rig reporting only that one fact still earns nothing.

creality_rs485.description: Creality RS-485 / CFS motor-bus traffic. The payload dumps are Python bytes reprs, so one substring on "b'\x" covers the whole family regardless of which message tag the firmware uses.

creality_k2_modules.description: Boot-time chatter from Creality's extras modules (model/version handshakes, IO remap, AI detection).

creality_macro_chatter.description: Per-move debug output from the Creality Klipper fork's own macros (park positions, nozzle clean, temp waits, driver currents).

klipper_verbose_probe.description: Per-point probe results during a bed mesh. Stock Klipper, not vendor-specific, and it is what you want to read while debugging a mesh - so no printer references this set by default.

probe_preparation.label: Zeroing load cell
probe_preparation.reason: ZMOD probes with a load cell whose zero drifts when bed screws or thermal preload change. ZMOD tares on its print path (_PREPARE_PRINT, _START_PRINT) but not on any calibration entry point, so an untared probe reports 'Probe triggered prior to movement'. BED_LEVEL_SCREWS_TUNE tares itself, hence skip_if_macro_in.

probe_preparation.label: Zeroing load cell
probe_preparation.reason: COSMOS probes with a load cell whose zero drifts between calibrations. Its load_cell module registers LOAD_CELL_TARE as a command, never a gcode_macro, so macro_match cannot see it: the load_cell_probe object keys the rule, and COSMOS's _COSMOS_SETTINGS macro keeps it off other firmware whose load cell may not define that command. COSMOS's BED_MESH_CALIBRATE tares the load cell itself, so bed mesh does not get it. Screws tilt does: the Elegoo Centauri Carbon entry's shipped sequence tares on its own and is self-preparing, and without COSMOS's wrapper the stock SCREWS_TILT_CALCULATE needs the tare from here.

printers.name: Voron 2.4
printers._print_start_default_phases_comment: Estimates for a 350mm-class gantry machine with a probe-based mesh: G28 plus a four-point QUAD_GANTRY_LEVEL (the 2.4 levels its gantry, never Z_TILT), then a mesh sweep, a brush wipe and a purge line. Heating is omitted - the thermal model owns those.

printers.name: Voron 0.2
printers._print_start_default_phases_comment: Estimates for a 120mm single-Z machine: no gantry to level and no three-point tilt, so G28 leads straight into a short mesh (when a probe is fitted), a wipe and a purge line. Heating is omitted - the thermal model owns those.

heuristics.reason: Quad Gantry Level present (Micron uses QGL like Voron 2.4)

printers.name: Voron Trident
printers._print_start_default_phases_comment: Estimates for a 350mm-class machine with a probe-based mesh: G28 plus a three-point Z_TILT_ADJUST (the Trident tilts its bed, it has no gantry to QGL), then a mesh sweep, a brush wipe and a purge line. Heating is omitted - the thermal model owns those.

printers.name: Voron Switchwire
printers._print_start_default_phases_comment: Estimates for a 250mm bed-slinger with a single Z and a probe-based mesh: neither a gantry to level nor a three-point tilt, so G28 leads into the mesh sweep, a wipe and a purge line. Heating is omitted - the thermal model owns those.

printers.name: Elegoo Centauri Carbon
printers._calibration_comment: COSMOS's BED_MESH_CALIBRATE is a macro that heats the bed to BED_TEMP, homes, cleans the nozzle, tares the load cell, probes, then measures the Z offset. It needs nothing sent ahead of it (bed_mesh_self_prepares); its M190/M109 wait for a hot bed to cool, so BED_TEMP never asks for less than a bed above 60C already has, even when a lower target is set. {profile_arg} stores the mesh under the chosen name as it completes; the Z-offset step clears the active mesh right after, so it cannot be saved from there.
printers._screws_tilt_comment: COSMOS replaces SCREWS_TILT_CALCULATE with a macro (rename_existing: SCREWS_TILT_CALCULATE_BASE) that tares the load cell, runs Klipper's calculation, parks, then opens a Manual Leveling prompt measuring every screw against a fixed bed height (z_bed_level + position_endstop - 4) rather than against a base screw. The shipped sequence is that macro without its prompt, so the Bed Screws panel shows Klipper's base-relative turns. Firmware without the wrapper runs the stock command, and the cosmos_load_cell_tare rule tares ahead of it.

calibration.screws_tilt_gcode:
LOAD_CELL_CALIBRATE TARE=TRUE SAVE=TRUE
{screws_tilt_builtin}
G90
G1 X128 Y220 Z20 F6000

printers._print_start_default_phases_comment: COSMOS PRINT_START, measured on a CC1 running 26.08 (2026-09-14, cold start, 105C bed / 260C nozzle): both heaters set without waiting, G28 through homing_override ~23s, M190, a heat soak of cosmos.conf heatsoak minutes (60s by default; cosmos_cc1.json holds the pre-print open for the minutes it announces), the stored default mesh loaded in under a second (adaptive_mesh probes a new mesh instead, which the history learns), SMART_PARK, M109, then a KAMP line purge ~13s. Heating is omitted: the thermal model owns it.
printers._thermal_rates_comment: Seconds per degree C for a first print, from the same COSMOS cold start: the bed took ~484s from 24.5C to 105C (about 4.3 s/C below 60C and 8 in the last 20C), the nozzle ~48s from 140C to 260C.

printers.name: Duender (MedusaHC)
printers.notes: Duender CoreXY (Irbis3D) fitted with the MedusaHC hotend changer. MedusaHC's own pin_watch extra and its Python controller's [medusahc] are scored here, with or without klipper-toolchanger beside them. Everything else (toolchanger/tool_count/corexy) describes any multi-tool CoreXY and would claim machines that are not this one. The bare-Duender hostname deliberately does NOT appear here, or the 'duender' entry could never outscore this one; a DuCR10 hostname is excluded instead, since the MedusaHC signals alone cannot tell the two frames apart.

printers.name: DuCR10 (MedusaHC)
printers.notes: DuCR10 CoreXY (Andizzle's 'DUO CR10' remix of the Irbis3D Duender, Printables 1263532) fitted with the MedusaHC hotend changer. Same MedusaHC signals as the Duender - only the hostname separates the two frames, so each entry excludes the other's hostname rather than competing on evidence that cannot tell them apart. The 'ducr10' hostname sits at 40 here deliberately: on a DuCR10 with no changer it must lose to the bare 'ducr10' entry (80), and it only ever adds the +3 extra-match bonus on top of a MedusaHC object match.

Hostname only, for the same reason as the 'duender' entry: the remix ships no Klipper config, and the one published build (topi314/klipper, branch ducr10) is a plain CoreXY with 3 Z steppers and a 210x210 bed mesh copied from the Duender - nothing there separates it from any other CoreXY, and a 'corexy' heuristic would compete with Voron and RatRig on every one of their machines.
